99	## Manifests (`render.go`, `manifests/`)
100	
101	`Render(p Params) ([]byte, error)` calls `p.Validate()` first (an invalid value
102	returns Validate's error, naming its variable, and no bytes) and writes a
103	multi-document YAML stream separated by `---`, in this order: Namespace, PVC,
104	Deployment, Service. `RenderNamespace(p)` returns the first document alone, so
105	that `up` can apply the Namespace before the rest. The output is deterministic
106	(no map iteration, no timestamp); the golden of the defaults is
107	`testdata/render-default.golden.yaml`, rewritten with
108	`go test ./internal/nexusbench -run TestRenderGolden -update` and reviewed as a
109	diff.
110	
111	| File (`go:embed`, `text/template`) | Object |
112	|---|---|
113	| `00-namespace.yaml.tmpl` | Namespace, labels `app.kubernetes.io/managed-by` and `part-of` = `devdesk-nexus-bench`; no `pod-security.kubernetes.io/*` label |
114	| `10-pvc.yaml.tmpl` | PVC `nexus-data`, `ReadWriteOnce`, `StorageSize`, no `storageClassName` (the cluster default class, `local-path`) |
115	| `20-deployment.yaml.tmpl` | Deployment `nexus`: 1 replica, `Recreate`, one container (`ImageRef`), ports `http` 8081 and `docker-group` 8082, requests and limits, env `INSTALL4J_ADD_VM_PARAMS`, PVC on `/nexus-data`, `startupProbe` on `/service/rest/v1/status` (10 s x 60 = 10 min), `readinessProbe` (same path), no `livenessProbe`, UID and GID 200, `runAsNonRoot`, no privilege escalation, `drop: [ALL]`, `RuntimeDefault` seccomp, no service account token, no service links |
116	| `30-service.yaml.tmpl` | Service `nexus`, `NodePort`: `http` 8081 to `HTTPNodePort`, `docker-group` 8082 to `DockerNodePort` |
117	
118	Quoting: the templates see only a `manifestData` built from validated values,
119	and every string goes through the `q` template function (`strconv.Quote`, a
120	valid YAML double-quoted scalar), so `true`, `null`, `123`, `0x1F`, `12:30:45` or
121	`2001-01-23` in `NEXUS_BENCH_JVM_OPTS` decode as strings (`TestRenderRoundTripsTrickyJVMOpts`,
122	`TestRenderQuotesEveryValue`). Quoted: namespace, image reference, JVM options,
123	CPU and memory quantities, storage size. Not quoted: the two NodePorts (integers),
124	and the literals of the template (names, labels, container ports).
125	
126	What the render does not carry: the context, the upstream URL, `Anonymous`,
127	`AcceptEULA`, `Hosts`, timeouts and paths (a change of any of them leaves the
128	bytes unchanged, `TestRenderIgnoresParamsTheManifestsDoNotCarry`); no Secret, no
129	ConfigMap, no `envFrom` or `valueFrom`, no hostPath, no object of cluster scope
130	but the Namespace; the word `password` or `secret` never appears. The admin
131	password is read from the pod and written to the secrets file by the
132	provisioning step, not by a manifest.
133	
134	## Errors, runner and preflight (`errors.go`, `kubectl.go`, `preflight.go`)
135	
136	**Errors.** Every failure of the bench is a `*BenchError{Kind, Cause, Check, Err}`.
137	`Error()` is `"<Cause>. Check: <Check>"`: a probable cause and what to run or look
138	at (a `kubectl` command, or a `mise` task), in English. `Err` is kept for
139	`errors.Is`/`errors.As` and is never printed: the text of a failed sub-process can
140	carry a credential, and neither the stderr of kubectl nor its error reaches a
141	message. `ErrKind` holds the kinds of D-F in the order the bench meets them:
142	`KubectlMissing`, `ContextNotFound`, `ClusterUnreachable`, `Forbidden`,
143	`NamespaceForeign`, `NamespaceMissing`, `NodePortTaken`, `AdmissionDenied`,
144	`PodPending`, `ImagePull`, `Crash`, `Deadline`, `RESTUnreachable`,
145	`ProvisionFailed`. The zero value is `Unclassified`, so an error nobody classified
146	never passes for a named kind. The last six are for the steps to come.
147	
148	`classifyKubectl(stderr)` is the fallback for what the exit status and the JSON
149	cannot tell apart; kubectl's wording changes between versions, so it matches
150	lower-cased fragments and returns `Unclassified` for an unknown text. Order of the
151	rules: an admission webhook that denied (even reported as `Forbidden`) is
152	`AdmissionDenied`; `provided port is already allocated` or `... not in the valid
153	range` is `NodePortTaken`; `forbidden` is `Forbidden`; `Unable to connect to the
154	server`, `connection refused`, `i/o timeout`, `TLS handshake timeout` are
155	`ClusterUnreachable`.
156	
157	**Runner.** `Runner.Run(ctx, stdin, args...)` returns both streams even on
158	failure. `NewExecRunner(context)` finds `kubectl` with `exec.LookPath` (a
159	`KubectlMissing` error otherwise, which names `kubectl` and `mise install`) and
160	puts `--context <context>` before every call, so callers never pass it.
161	`kubectl.go` is the only non-test file of the package that starts `kubectl`; the one other process is the `git check-ignore` of the secrets store (see below).
162	
163	**Preflight.** `RunPreflight(ctx, r, p, op) (PreflightResult, error)` with `op` one
164	of `OpUp`, `OpProvision`, `OpDown`, `OpStatus`. Checks, in this order, stopping at
165	the first failure:
166	
167	1. `p.Validate()`: invalid parameters are refused before any call.
168	2. `kubectl config get-contexts -o name`: the exact context name is listed, else
169	   `ContextNotFound`. Nothing else is asked.
170	3. `kubectl get --raw /readyz`: the API server answers, else `ClusterUnreachable`;
171	   a refusal (stderr `forbidden`: expired token, 403) is `Forbidden` instead, through
172	   the same `classifyKubectl` as every other call.
173	4. `kubectl auth can-i <verb> <resource>` (`-n <ns>`, `-A` or nothing):
174	   `up` needs create and patch `namespaces` (cluster; a server-side apply is a
175	   PATCH, also on a second run), create `persistentvolumeclaims`, `services`,
176	   `deployments` and `pods/exec` (namespace), list `services` (`-A`),
177	   patch `deployments`, `services` and `persistentvolumeclaims`, and get and list
178	   `pods` and `persistentvolumeclaims` (the wait of `Deploy`), all in the
179	   namespace (no manifest creates a Secret, so none is asked);
180	   `provision` needs create `pods/exec`, get `deployments` and list `pods`
181	   (namespace); `down` needs delete `namespaces`; `status`
182	   asks nothing. A `no` arrives on stdout with a non-zero exit, so stdout is read
183	   first: `Forbidden`, naming the verb and the resource.
184	5. `kubectl get namespace <ns> -o json`: absent is fine for `up` and `down` (nothing
185	   to delete) and `NamespaceMissing` for `provision` and `status`; present
186	   without the label `app.kubernetes.io/managed-by=devdesk-nexus-bench` is
187	   `NamespaceForeign` for every operation (the plan lists `up` and `down`;
188	   `provision` and `status` refuse too, so the bench never runs `exec` in a
189	   namespace it did not create).
190	6. `up` only, `kubectl get services -A -o json`: a Service other than `nexus` of
191	   our namespace that holds `HTTPNodePort` or `DockerNodePort` is `NodePortTaken`,
192	   naming `<namespace>/<name>` and the port. Our own Service is accepted, which is
193	   what makes a second `up` possible.
194	7. Everything but `down`, `kubectl get nodes -o json`: `NodeIP` is the first
195	   `InternalIP`; none is not an error (`NodeIP` stays empty).
196	
197	A call that fails in a way the checks above did not expect goes through
198	`classifyKubectl` (a `forbidden` stderr becomes `Forbidden`, anything unknown
199	`Unclassified`). Every call that reaches the API server carries
200	`--request-timeout=10s`.
201	
202	**No write before the end of the preflight.** The preflight issues `config`,
203	`get` and `auth can-i` only, never sends stdin, and a failure at any point leaves
204	the cluster untouched. The tests run it against a scripted fake runner that fails
205	the test on any call outside the six above and records every write verb
206	(`apply`, `create`, `delete`, `patch`, `exec`, ...) it would have seen. The
207	`Runner` of the later steps (apply, delete) is only called after `RunPreflight`
208	returned without an error.
209	
210	## Secrets and descriptor (`secrets.go`, `descriptor.go`)
211	
212	**Secrets.** `Secrets{AdminPassword, PendingAdminPassword, PullPassword}` (JSON
213	`adminPassword`, `pendingAdminPassword`, `pullPassword`; the last two are omitted
214	when empty) is kept by a `SecretStore` (`Load`, `Save`, `Remove`), implemented by
215	`NewFileStore(path)`. `PendingAdminPassword` is the new admin password, written
216	before it is sent to Nexus, so an interrupted change loses nothing.
217	
218	- Path: `DefaultSecretsPath(context, namespace, getenv)` is
219	  `$XDG_STATE_HOME/devdesk/nexus-bench/<context>/<namespace>/secrets.json`, else
220	  `$HOME/.local/state/...` (`USERPROFILE` when `HOME` is unset); an empty variable
221	  counts as unset, none of them set is an error, and `NEXUS_BENCH_SECRETS`
222	  overrides the whole path. It is outside every repository and shared by all the
223	  worktrees, so a worktree never keeps a stale admin password of its own.
224	- Modes: the file is `0600`, the folders `Save` creates are `0700`. The write is
225	  atomic (`writeFileAtomic`): a temporary file in the same folder, `chmod`, sync,
226	  rename, then a best-effort sync of the folder so the new name survives a power
227	  cut (errors ignored: Windows and some file systems cannot sync a folder); the
228	  temporary file is removed when anything fails, so a failed `Save`
229	  leaves no partial file and a file left by someone else with a wider mode is
230	  replaced, not kept. POSIX modes are not meaningful on Windows (the test skips).
231	- File name: `NewFileStore` refuses a path whose file name is not `secrets.json`
232	  (`Remove` deletes that file, and a mistyped `NEXUS_BENCH_SECRETS` must not point
233	  it at `~/.ssh/id_ed25519`).
234	- Mode on read: `Load` refuses a file with a group or other bit (`mode & 0o077`),
235	  outside Windows, with a `BenchError` that never shows the content and says
236	  `chmod 600 <path>`.
237	- Display: `Secrets` has `String`, `GoString` and `LogValue` methods that all give
238	  `Secrets{redacted}`, so no fmt verb (`%v`, `%+v`, `%#v`, `%s`, `%q`) and no slog
239	  handler prints a password (`TestSecretsAreRedactedWhenFormatted`). The JSON of
240	  the file is unaffected.
241	- `Load` returns `(zero, false, nil)` when the file is absent. A file that is not a
242	  valid JSON object is a `BenchError` that names the path and never shows the
243	  content (the underlying error is kept in `Err`, which is not printed).
244	- `Remove` deletes the file, then the namespace folder when it is empty; it
245	  succeeds when there is nothing to remove, and a folder holding anything else
246	  stays.
247	- Git guard: `NewFileStore` refuses an empty path and touches nothing on disk.
248	  It walks up from the file's folder looking for a `.git` entry (directory or
249	  file, so a worktree counts); with none, the path is accepted without asking
250	  git. With one, it runs `git -C <root> check-ignore -q -- <path>`: ignored is
251	  accepted; not ignored, or git unavailable, is a `BenchError` that says to set
252	  `NEXUS_BENCH_SECRETS` outside the repository. The process runs with the caller's
253	  environment minus `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, `GIT_COMMON_DIR`,
254	  `GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY`, `GIT_NAMESPACE`, `GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES`,
255	  `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS`, `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT`, `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_*`,
256	  `GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_*`, `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`, `GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM` and
257	  `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM` (`gitEnvironment`), then `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=<devnull>` and
258	  `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1`, so the verdict is about the repository of the path and
259	  its own ignore rules, not about a repository or a `core.excludesFile` the
260	  caller's variables or configuration point at (a path ignored only by a global
261	  excludes file is therefore refused). That call is the only process
262	  outside `kubectl.go`; it lives in the package variable `gitIgnores`, so it can
263	  be replaced and found by a source guard.
264	
265	**Descriptor.** `BuildDescriptor(p, DeployResult, ProvisionResult)` returns the
266	`Descriptor` of schema 1 (D-D): `schemaVersion`, `kubeContext`, `namespace`,
267	`image`, `nexusVersion`, `edition`, `eulaAccepted`, `hosts`, `rest`,
268	`dockerConnectors`, `repositories`, `realms`, `accounts`, in that order, which is the
269	order of the struct fields. `hosts` is `Params.Hosts` when set, else `127.0.0.1`
270	then `DeployResult.NodeIP` when it is not empty; the URLs are `http://<host>:<nodePort>`
271	for each host (`RESTBaseURL(host, p)` is the exported REST origin: brackets for
272	IPv6, `%25` for a zone; the deployment, the descriptor and the command of step 8
273	all build it there). `DeployResult{ReachableHosts, NodeIP}` (step 4) and
274	`ProvisionResult{NexusVersion, Edition, EULAAccepted}` (step 6) are defined in
275	`descriptor.go` and reused by those steps. The account `anonymous` always
276	appears; its `enabled` is a `*bool`, so `false` is written when
277	`NEXUS_BENCH_ANONYMOUS=false`, and the other accounts write no `enabled`.
278	
279	- `WriteDescriptor(path, d)`: JSON indented by two spaces, one final newline, `0644`
280	  file, atomic through the same helper; the bytes depend on `d` alone.
281	- `LoadDescriptor(path)`: a missing file is `ErrNoDescriptor` (wrapped, use
282	  `errors.Is`); invalid JSON or a `schemaVersion` other than 1 (missing counts as 0)
283	  is an error that names the file and never shows its content.
284	- `DescriptorPath()`: `NEXUS_BENCH_DESCRIPTOR` when set and not empty, else
285	  `internal/nexusbench/descriptor.json`, found with `runtime.Caller`, so it does
286	  not depend on the working directory (and does not survive `-trimpath`).
287	- Never in the descriptor: a password or any secret, the path of the secrets file,
288	  a timestamp, a pod name, or the word `password` (`TestDescriptorHoldsNoSecret`,
289	  `TestDescriptorFormat`).
290	
291	The golden `testdata/descriptor.example.json` is the descriptor of `Defaults()`
292	with node IP `192.168.1.31`, Nexus `3.98.1-01`, `COMMUNITY`, EULA accepted. It is
293	checked both ways: `WriteDescriptor` must write exactly these bytes
294	(`TestDescriptorGolden`) and `LoadDescriptor` must read back `BuildDescriptor`'s
295	value (`TestLoadDescriptorGoldenMatchesBuild`). After a deliberate change of the
296	schema, regenerate it with
297	`go test ./internal/nexusbench -run TestDescriptorGolden -update` and review the
298	diff by hand (bump `schemaVersion` when a field changes meaning).
299	
300	## REST client and provisioning (`nexusapi.go`, `provision.go`, `initialpassword.go`)
301	
302	`Provision(ctx, baseURL, ip, store, p, out) (ProvisionResult, error)` brings a
303	running Nexus to the state the bench needs (D-E). `baseURL` is the REST origin
304	(no path); `ip` is an `InitialPassword` (`Read(ctx) (pw, ok, err)`); `out` gets
305	progress lines (`provision: ...`) and never a password.
306	
307	**Idempotence.** Every object is read, then created when absent or replaced when
308	present; there is no "create and ignore the error". A second run sends no `POST`
309	and changes neither the state nor any password. Order of the calls:
310	
311	1. `GET /v1/status` (no account): version and edition from the `Server` header
312	   (`Nexus/3.98.1-01 (COMMUNITY)`), else `info.version` of
313	   `/service/rest/swagger.json`, else empty (a note on `out`). The version is
314	   optional: a swagger answer that is a refusal or not JSON (a proxy page) leaves
315	   it empty; only a transport failure stops the run.
316	2. Admin credentials (below).
317	3. EULA: `GET /v1/system/eula`; 404 means an edition without one (noted,
318	   `EULAAccepted` false); `accepted: true` changes nothing; otherwise it is
319	   accepted only when `Params.AcceptEULA` (`NEXUS_BENCH_ACCEPT_EULA=yes`), with
320	   `POST {"accepted":true,"disclaimer":<as received>}`; the disclaimer is kept as
321	   a `json.RawMessage`, never rebuilt. Without consent `Provision` stops with a
322	   `ProvisionFailed` that names `NEXUS_BENCH_ACCEPT_EULA` and says that no
323	   repository, role or account was created, before any creation (the
324	   only write before it is the admin password change, which the EULA read needs).
325	4. Blob store: `GET /v1/blobstores` must list `default`, else `ProvisionFailed`
326	   before any role, user or repository is created.
327	5. Realms: `GET /v1/security/realms/active`; the missing ones of
328	   `NexusAuthenticatingRealm`, `DockerToken` are appended and the list is
329	   `PUT` back (a list that is already complete is not written). The plan said
330	   "set these two"; appending keeps a realm the instance already needs.
331	6. Anonymous access: `GET`, then always `PUT {"enabled": Params.Anonymous,
332	   "userId": "anonymous", "realmName": <current, default NexusAuthorizingRealm>}`.
333	7. Role `bench-docker-pull` (`nx-repository-view-docker-*-browse` and `-read`):
334	   `GET` 404 then `POST`, found then `PUT`.
335	8. User `bench-pull` (role above, status `active`): `GET /users?userId=bench-pull`,
336	   then `POST` with the password, or `PUT` plus `PUT .../change-password` with the
337	   stored password. The list filter matches by substring, so the element whose
338	   `userId` is exactly `bench-pull` is the one used.
339	9. `docker-hosted`, `docker-proxy` (`remoteUrl` = `Params.UpstreamURL`,
340	   `indexType: REGISTRY`) and `docker-group` (members hosted then proxy,
341	   `docker.httpPort: 8082`), all on blob store `default`, `forceBasicAuth: false`
342	   (anonymous pulls): `GET .../{name}` 404 then `POST`, found then `PUT`.
343	
344	**Admin credentials, a state machine with the write first.** `Load` the store;
345	the candidates are `adminPassword`, then `pendingAdminPassword`; an empty value
346	is never tried (a `{}` file means "not provided", and no request carries an empty
347	password). A candidate is accepted when `GET /v1/security/users?userId=admin`
348	answers 2xx; a 401 is a refusal and goes to the next candidate, any other status
349	is an error (a redirect or a 500 is not "wrong password"). A pending password
350	that the instance accepts is promoted to `adminPassword` with no new change.
351	When no candidate works, `InitialPassword.Read` supplies the password of the pod:
352	absent or refused gives the error `the bench admin password is unknown ...`, with
353	the check `mise run nexus-bench:down`, then `up`. Otherwise a password is
354	generated (or the stored pending one is reused), **`Save` stores it as
355	`pendingAdminPassword` first**, then `PUT /users/admin/change-password`
356	(`text/plain`) runs with the initial password, then `Save` promotes it to
357	`adminPassword`. A failed `Save` stops the run before the instance is touched
358	(`TestProvisionStopsWhenSaveFails`); a crash between the steps is resumed from the
359	pending password on the next run. The pull password follows the same rule: stored
360	before the user is created or its password set.
361	
362	**Generated passwords** are 32 characters of `[A-Za-z0-9]` from `crypto/rand`
363	(rejection sampling, no modulo bias), never a fixed or predictable value.
364	
365	**`kubectlInitialPassword`** (`NewKubectlInitialPassword(runner, namespace)`) runs
366	`-n <ns> exec deploy/nexus -- cat /nexus-data/admin.password` through the
367	`Runner`, so `kubectl.go` stays the only file that starts a process. A "No such
368	file or directory" on stderr is (empty, false, nil); another failure is a
369	`BenchError` (kind from `classifyKubectl`, else `ProvisionFailed`) whose message
370	holds neither stdout nor stderr. Unit-tested on a fake `Runner`; no integration
371	test.
372	
373	**Client** (`client`, `newClient(baseURL, user, password)`): a dedicated
374	`http.Client` with `Timeout` 15 s, no proxy (the environment's proxy would receive
375	the credentials), and a `CheckRedirect` that returns `http.ErrUseLastResponse`:
376	no redirection is followed, so the 3xx is the answer and the target is never
377	contacted or named. A 2xx answer is read through `io.LimitReader` at 1 MiB + 1;
378	more is a `tooLargeError` and the content is never decoded (exactly 1 MiB is
379	read). Basic auth is set per request, only when there is a user; no header is
380	logged.
381	
382	**Errors.** `*APIError{Op, Status}` prints `<Op>: HTTP <status> <text>`: no URL,
383	no request or answer body. `Provision` returns `*BenchError` only:
384	`RESTUnreachable` when a call got no answer, `ProvisionFailed` otherwise, with
385	the `*APIError` (or the store or pod error) in `Err` so `errors.As` and
386	`errors.Is` reach it. A 401 or 403 adds the hint that the stored admin password
387	may not match. No error and no line on `out` holds a password
388	(`TestProvisionNeverPrintsAPassword`, and `requireQuiet` after every scenario,
389	which knows every password the fake saw).
390	
391	**H-REST: unverified hypotheses.** The in-memory Nexus of `fakenexus_test.go`
392	(`httptest`, loopback) is the one place that knows the JSON shapes, and it was
393	written from the Sonatype documentation, not from an instance. To check against
394	`/service/rest/swagger.json` at step 10, and to fix in the fake and the client
395	together:
396	
397	- the `Server` header on `/v1/status`, and the swagger fallback;
398	- the EULA payload and the `404` of an edition without one;
399	- `change-password` as `text/plain`, and whether `admin.password` is deleted once
400	  the password is changed through the API;
401	- the realm ids (`DockerToken`) and that the active list can be read and `PUT`;
402	- the anonymous payload (`enabled`, `userId`, `realmName`);
403	- the role and user payloads (`source` only on `PUT`, `externalRoles`), and a
404	  `userId` filter that matches by substring;
405	- the repository payloads (`storage`, `docker`, `proxy`, `dockerProxy`,
406	  `negativeCache`, `httpClient`, `group.memberNames`, `docker.httpPort`), the
407	  statuses of `POST` (201) and `PUT` (204), the path-routing field added in 3.83
408	  (left to the default of Nexus), and a proxy created before its upstream exists.
409	
410	**Security guarantees.** No redirect followed; answers bounded; no proxy; no
411	`Authorization` header, URL with credentials, body or password in any error or
412	output; passwords written to the store before use; an empty password never sent;
413	no process started outside `kubectl.go`.
414	
415	## Destruction and the clock (`destroy.go`, `clock.go`)
416	
417	`Destroy(ctx, runner, clock, store, params, out)` is the one irreversible
418	operation of the bench (risk R1), so its order is fixed:
419	
420	1. `RunPreflight(OpDown)`: `Validate` first (no call at all), then context,
421	   `/readyz`, `auth can-i delete namespaces`, and the namespace. A namespace
422	   without the label `app.kubernetes.io/managed-by=devdesk-nexus-bench` is
423	   refused here with `NamespaceForeign`, before any write.
424	2. A namespace that is absent prints `nothing to delete` and succeeds. The
425	   stored secrets are removed anyway, so a stale `secrets.json` does not
426	   outlive its bench and a second `down` is idempotent.
427	3. **One write**: `delete namespace <ns> --wait=false`, issued once, never
428	   retried (a `Forbidden` is returned as is). Nothing else is ever written: no
429	   finalizer patch, no force delete, no delete of another object. The tests
430	   journal every call and fail on a second write.
431	4. The namespace is read (`get namespace <ns> -o json`) until `NotFound` or
432	   `NEXUS_BENCH_DELETE_TIMEOUT` (default 3 min). The first read is immediate; the
433	   interval between reads doubles from 1 s to 10 s, always through `Clock.Sleep`
434	   and clipped to what remains of the timeout. A namespace stuck in `Terminating`
435	   ends in a `Deadline` error that cites the namespace, `spec.finalizers` and
436	   each `status.conditions` entry (type, status, message); the bench does not
437	   remove them.
438	5. One read of `get pv -o json`. A PersistentVolume whose `claimRef.namespace` is
439	   the bench namespace prints a line starting with `warning:` that names it and
440	   its phase and says it still exists: the run still succeeds, because the
441	   reclaim policy decides (`Delete` may remove it seconds later, `Retain` keeps
442	   the data on the node) and the bench does not delete a volume itself. No such volume, no
443	   warning. A PV list that cannot be read is also a warning, not a failure.
444	6. `store.Remove()`, last, and only when the namespace is gone. Its failure is
445	   returned as a `BenchError` (the namespace is already deleted; running `down`
446	   again retries the removal). A failed or cancelled run never touches the
447	   secrets.
448	
449	A cancelled context ends the wait with an error that wraps `context.Canceled`
450	(`errors.Is` holds); the namespace keeps terminating on the cluster. Lines on
451	`out` start with `down:` and, like every error, hold no password.
452	
453	`Clock` (`Now`, `Sleep(ctx, d) error`) is how the waits spend time. `NewClock()`
454	is the wall clock: `Sleep` returns `ctx.Err()` when the context is done (before
455	sleeping, even for a zero duration), returns at once for `d <= 0`, and otherwise
456	waits on a timer or the context. `fakeClock` of `clock_test.go` moves its time
457	forward instead of waiting, so no test sleeps for real.
458	
459	## Deployment and the wait (`deploy.go`, `probe.go`)
460	
461	`Deploy(ctx, runner, prober, clock, params, out) (DeployResult, error)` applies
462	the manifests and waits until Nexus answers. Order, fixed:
463	
464	1. `RunPreflight(OpUp)`, whole; no write before it succeeds.
465	2. `ctx` is looked at (a runner may ignore it), then
466	   `kubectl apply --server-side --field-manager=devdesk-nexus-bench -f -` with
467	   `RenderNamespace(p)` on stdin: the Namespace alone, so a failure later leaves
468	   at worst our labeled namespace and never anything outside it.
469	3. The same apply with `Render(p)`: the whole stream, the Namespace again
470	   included. A second `up` sends the same two applies and gets the same result;
471	   `--prune` is never used.
472	4. The wait, one round per `pollInterval` (5 s) through `Clock.Sleep`: read
473	   `get pods -n <ns> -l app.kubernetes.io/name=nexus -o json` and
474	   `get pvc -n <ns> -o json`, diagnose them, then probe every host. The deadline
475	   is `NEXUS_BENCH_TIMEOUT` (10 min); it is checked after a round, so the cluster
476	   is read once more at the very end.
477	
478	**Failure of an apply** is classified from its stderr by `classifyKubectl`:
479	`NodePortTaken` (names `NEXUS_BENCH_HTTP_NODEPORT` and `..._DOCKER_NODEPORT`),
480	`AdmissionDenied` (a webhook refusal wins over the `Forbidden` the API server
481	also reports), `Forbidden`, `ClusterUnreachable`, else `Unclassified`. The
482	runner's error is the `Err` of the `BenchError` (for `errors.Is`); neither the
483	stderr nor the error of the prober is ever in a message. After a failed apply
484	nothing else is called: no read, no probe, no sleep.
485	
486	**Diagnosis**, each round, on the pods that are not being deleted:
487	
488	| Reading | Kind | When |
489	|---|---|---|
490	| container waiting on `ErrImagePull` or `ImagePullBackOff` | `ImagePull` (names the image and `NEXUS_BENCH_IMAGE`, `_IMAGE_TAG`) | at once |
491	| `CrashLoopBackOff`, or `OOMKilled` as last or current termination | `Crash` (names the memory limit and `NEXUS_BENCH_MEMORY_LIMIT`) | at once |
492	| `PodScheduled=False`, reason `Unschedulable`, message with `Insufficient memory` or `Insufficient cpu` | `PodPending` (the request and `NEXUS_BENCH_MEMORY_REQUEST` or `_CPU_REQUEST`) | after `pendingGrace` (30 s) |
493	| claim `Pending` while a pod is scheduled | `PodPending` (the size and `NEXUS_BENCH_STORAGE_SIZE`) | after `pendingGrace` |
494	| no host answers by the deadline | `Deadline` (last state of the pod and the claim, the hosts tried, `NEXUS_BENCH_TIMEOUT`) | at `Params.Timeout` |
495	
496	The unschedulable pod is read before the claim: while the pod is not scheduled, a
497	claim of a `WaitForFirstConsumer` class is `Pending` for that reason alone and is
498	not blamed. A reading that changes or disappears restarts the grace count (the
499	volume binds when the pod is scheduled; the Deployment may have made no pod yet).
500	When the deadline arrives with such a reading still active, it is returned as
501	`PodPending` rather than `Deadline`. A cancelled context is returned as is
502	(`errors.Is(err, context.Canceled)`), never as a `Deadline`.
503	
504	**Reached hosts.** The hosts are `Params.Hosts` when set, else `127.0.0.1` and
505	the node `InternalIP` (when there is one). Each round probes them in parallel at
506	`http://<host>:<HTTPNodePort>` (`net.JoinHostPort`, so IPv6 gets brackets) and
507	returns after the first round in which at least one answered, with
508	`DeployResult.ReachableHosts` = the hosts that answered in that round, in host
509	order. A host that did not answer then gets a line on `out` that starts with
510	`deploy: warning:` and names it; no warning when all answered. `BuildDescriptor`
511	lists in `hosts` (and in every URL) `Params.Hosts` when set, else
512	`ReachableHosts` when not empty, else the earlier fallback (`127.0.0.1` and
513	`NodeIP`), so the descriptor never promises a host that did not answer
514	(`descriptor_hosts_test.go`).
515	
516	**Prober** (`probe.go`): `NewProber()` is one unauthenticated `GET
517	<baseURL>/service/rest/v1/status` on a dedicated client (5 s timeout, no proxy,
518	no keep-alive, `CheckRedirect` returning `http.ErrUseLastResponse`): nil on 200
519	and only then, otherwise a `*APIError` (status only) or a `*transportError`
520	(wrapping the cause for `errors.Is`). The body is neither read for its content
521	nor reported, and a redirect target is never contacted.
522	
523	**Rights the deployment needs** (all asked by the preflight, namespace-scoped
524	except the first two): create and patch `namespaces` (cluster); create and patch
525	`persistentvolumeclaims`, `services`, `deployments`; get and list `pods` and
526	`persistentvolumeclaims`; create `pods/exec` (used by `Provision`); list `services` in all namespaces (NodePort check).
527	
528	**Not covered by the fakes.** `Deploy` has only run against a scripted `Runner`,
529	a fake `Prober` and a fake `Clock`; the real kubectl output shape of
530	`get pods -o json` (container status fields), the real duration of the pull and
531	the start, and whether `kubectl apply --server-side` of a Namespace that carries
532	no field of its own conflicts on a second run are for step 10.
533	
534	## Residual risks (security audit of the steps 4, 6, 7)
535	
536	Known and accepted for a throw-away bench; none is fixed by this change.
537	
538	- **Basic credentials in clear HTTP.** Nexus is reached on `http://`, so the admin
539	  and `bench-pull` credentials of `Provision` travel unencrypted. The command of
540	  step 8 must prefer `127.0.0.1` (`RESTBaseURL("127.0.0.1", p)`) and send
541	  credentials to the node IP only on an explicit option of the operator. This is
542	  a commitment for step 8, not something the package enforces.
543	- **`local-path` volume in `0777`.** The data folder of the local-path
544	  provisioner is world-writable, so `admin.password` is readable by every local
545	  account of the node between the start of Nexus and the provisioning (which
546	  changes it).
547	- **NodePorts on the LAN, anonymous access on purpose.** The two NodePorts listen
548	  on every interface of the node, and anonymous access is enabled by default so
549	  that pulls need no login (`NEXUS_BENCH_ANONYMOUS`). Anyone on the LAN can read
550	  the bench; do not put anything private in it.
551	- **Mutable image tag.** The image is `docker.io/sonatype/nexus3:<tag>` with no
552	  digest: the same tag can resolve to another image later.
553	- **Partial result on error.** `Provision` returns the `ProvisionResult` it had
554	  gathered together with the error. The command must not write the descriptor
555	  when `err != nil`, or it would describe a bench that is half provisioned.
556	
557	## Still to come
558	
559	The `nexus-bench` command and mise tasks (8), guarded integration
560	tests and source guards (9), and the first real run on `datomir` (10, blocked on
561	the EULA and cluster-access decisions Q1 and Q2 of the plan). This file grows
562	with each step.
563

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **AI Collaboration Rule**:
> - **Planning**, **Brainstorming**, **Implementation** and **Bug fixes** are all
>   in scope. Planning is no longer delegated to Gemini (Antigravity).
> - Implementation plans go in `.claude/plans/` (see
>   [rules/planning.md](rules/planning.md)); design decisions that outlive a plan
>   are recorded in `docs/backlog.md`. Open work (stories, tasks, bugs) is tracked
>   in Plane, see the `## Plane` section of the root `CLAUDE.md`.
> - Always refer to [project-context.md](../project-context.md) for global project rules.
>   It sits in this repository, at the root. The absolute path this line used to
>   carry named a GitLab checkout that is no longer where DevDesk lives.

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only) + a path trace under Diagnostics (Trace Path button, or `H` on the route row; no separate tab since DEVDESK-471) (native path trace, on native Linux, native Windows (IPv4 only, ICMP echoes through `iphlpapi`, DEVDESK-486) and WSL2: on macOS and WSL1 the button, `H`, `enter` and `ctrl+o` are greyed and the footer says why, DEVDESK-334; the column starts with this machine, its interface and its gateway; `ctrl+o` can start it from a running Docker Engine container instead (container and network rows, hops still traced from this machine); `H` on the Diagnostics route row opens the trace level on that host without starting it (greyed with the reason on an unsupported platform or a target the trace refuses; its interface and gateway rows reuse the Local route check's reading of the same address, read once, DEVDESK-473), and in the trace level `enter` starts or restarts it, `ctrl+o` picks the source, `esc` cancels then goes back where it came from; under WSL2 the source row says `WSL2 (VM), not the Windows host` with the networking mode, and in NAT mode the gateway and TTL 1 hop are tagged `Windows host (virtual switch)` only when proven, DEVDESK-333; the interface row says `no route` when the kernel proves there is none and `undetermined` when the routing table could not be read, a no-route error keeps the local rows, a trace that ends on the hop limit or the deadline folds its silent tail into one `silent` row and marks the `last to answer` hop, and the target refuses a `:port`, DEVDESK-335)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line) shown as a status dot in the first column (the `running` dot blinks, DEVDESK-151) and as text, tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost` (orange from 75 % and red from 90 % of the session's estimated cost, when at least two agents are priced), from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, when its transcript is gone, or while the terminal is not focused (header `Updates › paused`, then `paused (terminal not focused)`; `app.when_unfocused: run` keeps it live); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. The sessions list itself is not live.

## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

```bash
# Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go
mise run ci           # the six checks in order (fmt-check, vet, lint, build, test, test-race), stops at the first failure; unlike check it rewrites no file and also runs build and test-race. CI itself runs only fmt-check, vet, lint and build: tests are disabled in CI (maintainer decision, D149), so run this locally before every PR

# Installation
mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
```

`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.

## Releases

Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

**Test input and colour (DEVDESK-199).** Build keys only through
`internal/ui/testutil` (`Key`, `Keys`, `Type`, `Paste`, `Text`, `IsText`), never a
literal `tea.KeyPressMsg` or `tea.Key*`. `Key` returns a
`tea.KeyPressMsg` (`Keys` and `Type` return a message list), `Paste` a `tea.PasteMsg`; `Key` is strict: an unknown name
panics. The space key is built as a key (`Key("space")`), never matched through
`String()` (v1 `" "`, v2 `"space"`). Lip Gloss v2 has no global colour profile (`Style.Render` always emits full
colour), so a test needs no setup to check styling; it reads the SGR or strips it
with `ansi.Strip`. `internal/ui/testutil/source_guard_test.go` fails the suite on a
hand-built key, a `colorprofile` import outside `internal/app/profile_test.go` and
`internal/app/redraw_measure_test.go` or `SetColorProfile` in any `_test.go`. Paste tests
(`internal/app/paste_test.go`, `wrapped_input_test.go`, `component_form_test.go`):
a paste reaches the focused field, newlines become spaces in single-line fields,
and no key action fires (Rule 111).

**Space and key API (DEVDESK-200).** Production code matches the space key as
`keymap.Space`, never `" "`/`"space"`, and reads keys through `String()` only
(no `.Runes`, `.Alt`, `.Paste`, `tea.KeyType` or `tea.Key<Name>`). Update
handlers switch on `tea.KeyPressMsg`, never the `tea.KeyMsg` interface (it also
matches releases). A paste is a `tea.PasteMsg`, not a key (Rule 111). Guards in
`internal/ui/keymap` (`space_scan_test.go`, `legacy_key_scan_test.go`,
`viewport_keymap_scan_test.go`) fail the suite otherwise; limits are listed in
`docs/architecture/app-shell.md`.

## Critical Bubble Tea Rules

**NEVER modify model state inside a Cmd** (Rule 110) - Race condition:
- `Update()` is the ONLY place to modify model state
- `View()` is read-only
- `Cmd` functions do I/O and return messages

**NEVER use `style.Render()` inside `table.Row{}`** (Rule 122) - ANSI sequences corrupt all subsequent rows:
- Use plain text: `theme.IconError + " error"` not `theme.StatusErrorStyle.Render(...)`
- Apply row styling via `table.SetStyles(theme.TableStylesForState("error"))`

**Views render through `Render()`** (Bubble Tea v2): a top-level view implements
`Render() string` and `View() tea.View { return tea.NewView(m.Render()) }`; only the
router (`App.View()`) sets terminal state such as `AltScreen` and `BackgroundColor`. Components keep
`View() string`. Colours are `color.Color`; hex literals stay in `theme/colors.go`.

**Update() case extraction**: If a case block exceeds 5 lines, extract to `handle[MessageType]()` method returning `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)`

## Critical rules (summary)

**Rule 110** — NEVER modify the model inside a `Cmd` → race condition. Only `Update()` modifies the model.

**Rule 122** — `Cell` returns plain text (it gets measured), color goes through `Style`. A `style.Render(...)` inside `Cell` gets truncated in the middle of its escape sequence and bleeds onto every following row.

**Rule 128** — A footer message goes through `components.FooterMessage`: three levels (neutral info, orange warning, red error), always centered, a single implementation. A table's loading state is shown in the footer, never in the body: with the shared activity dot (`Status.Activity`, `●`/`○`, `SetBlinkPhase`), for a view's own load as well as for work the router tracks. The braille spinner API is removed (DEVDESK-377): nothing under `internal/` imports `bubbles/v2/spinner` or names `Status.Spinner`, `SetSpinnerFrame`, `theme.SpinnerMessage` or `theme.SpinnerStyle` (`TestNoViewImportsTheBubblesSpinner`, `TestRemovedSpinnerSymbolsStayGone`), with no exception. A new `Activity` value not driven by the jobs registry must implement `WantsBlink()`, or the dot stays fixed.

**Rule 139** — A `datatable`'s body is always `m.table.View()`, never a loading screen or a message: an empty table (loading, nothing to list, a filter with no results) stays a table — a header, no rows. The count goes in `GetHeaderInfo`, the status in the footer.

**Rule 129** — All UI text and all logs in **English US**.

**Rule 140** — An invalid form field is underlined through `theme.StyleInvalidField` (the only entry point to the underline API), and the error is also in the footer at level Error, derived on every render. The underline is never the only carrier.

**Rule 133** — `bubbles/textarea` is forbidden. Use `components.WrappedInput` for any multi-line text field.

The per-topic TUI rule files above load when a matching file is read or edited; when reviewing a diff without opening files, read them explicitly.

## Code quality rules and proactive checks

### Rule 301 : Systematic code quality check before commit

**MANDATORY**: Before creating a commit, ALWAYS perform the following checks:

#### 1. Go linter (golangci-lint)
```bash
golangci-lint run
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Fix ALL warnings and errors
- ✅ Specifically check deprecation warnings (SA1019)
- ✅ NEVER ignore warnings without documented justification

#### 2. Tests
```bash
go test ./...
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Verify that all tests pass
- ✅ If tests fail, fix them BEFORE the commit

#### 3. Build
```bash
go build
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Verify that the build succeeds without errors
- ✅ Test the application if functional changes were made

#### 4. Deprecated dependencies

**Detection:**
- Check golangci-lint SA1019 warnings
- Look in go.mod for packages marked as deprecated

**Action:**
- Replace IMMEDIATELY with a maintained alternative
- Document the replacement in the commit message
- Update the documentation (.claude/CLAUDE.md)

**Examples of common replacements:**
- `github.com/go-ping/ping` → `github.com/prometheus-community/pro-bing`

### Rule 302 : IDE diagnostics check

**MANDATORY**: Before each commit, check the IDE diagnostics:

```
Use mcp__ide__getDiagnostics to check:
- Compilation errors
- Unused parameters
- Unused imports
- Other warnings
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Fix or justify every diagnostic
- ✅ Do not ignore "unused parameter" without a reason

### Rule 303 : go.mod and dependencies

**After any dependency change:**

```bash
go mod tidy
go mod verify
```

**Required actions:**
- ✅ Verify that go.mod is up to date
- ✅ Verify that go.sum is consistent
- ✅ Document new dependencies in .claude/CLAUDE.md

### Rule 304 : Quality commit message

**Mandatory format for quality fixes — in English (see Rule 307):**

```
type: short description

Detailed description explaining:
- What was detected (warning, error, etc.)
- Why it was a problem
- How it was resolved

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
```

**Commit types for quality:**
- `fix:` - Bug fix detected by linter
- `chore:` - Deprecated dependency replacement
- `refactor:` - Code quality improvement

### Rule 305 : MANDATORY pre-commit checklist

**Before EVERY commit, check:**

- [ ] `golangci-lint run` → 0 warnings
- [ ] `go test ./...` → PASS
- [ ] `go build` → SUCCESS
- [ ] `mcp__ide__getDiagnostics` → No critical error
- [ ] `go.mod` up to date (if dependencies changed)
- [ ] Documentation updated (if API changed)
- [ ] Tests added (if new feature)

**If EVEN ONE of these checks fails:**
- ❌ DO NOT create the commit
- ✅ Fix it first
- ✅ Restart the checklist

### Rule 306 : MANDATORY proactivity

**Claude Code MUST:**
- ✅ Check the linter WITHOUT the user asking
- ✅ Propose fixes BEFORE the commit
- ✅ Flag deprecated dependencies AS SOON AS they are detected
- ✅ Document all quality changes

**Claude Code MUST NEVER:**
- ❌ Wait for the user to flag a warning
- ❌ Create a commit with unresolved warnings
- ❌ Ignore dependency issues
- ❌ Forget to update the documentation

### Correct workflow examples

**Example 1 - Feature commit:**
```
1. Write the code
2. go build → verify compilation
3. golangci-lint run → fix warnings
4. go test ./... → verify tests
5. mcp__ide__getDiagnostics → check the IDE
6. git commit with a detailed message
```

**Example 2 - Detecting a deprecated dependency:**
```
1. golangci-lint detects SA1019
2. Look up the recommended alternative
3. Replace the import and the code
4. go mod tidy
5. Test that everything works
6. Update .claude/CLAUDE.md
7. git commit explaining the replacement
```

### Rule 307 : Commits and code comments — English only

**Every git commit message and every comment in the code must be written
in English**, regardless of the language used to converse with the user.

| Element | Language |
|---------|--------|
| Commit message (title + body) | ✅ English only |
| Code comment (`//`, `/* */`, docstring) | ✅ English only |
| Replies to the user in the conversation | The user's language (see memory `feedback-langue-francais`) |
| UI and logs (Rule 129) | English US only — already covered, unchanged |

This **replaces** the earlier tolerance listed in `.claude/CLAUDE.md` under
"Code Conventions" ("Comments: French or English both accepted"): existing
French comments are not to be rewritten wholesale, but any new comment and
any edit to an existing comment must be in English.

```
// ✅ CORRECT
// retry with backoff because the API rate-limits bursts above 10 req/s

// ❌ WRONG (a French comment, which Rule 307 forbids)
// on relance avec un backoff car l'API limite les rafales au-delà de 10 req/s
```

```
✅ fix: correct table width calculation when a column is dropped

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

❌ fix: corrige le calcul de largeur de colonne
```

Forbidden:
- ❌ A commit message written in French, even partially
- ❌ A new code comment in French
- ❌ Confusing this rule with the language of the conversation, which
  remains the user's

## Code editing instructions

### Rule 201 : Code must be clean, concise, and well-structured to stay maintainable

#### Extracting functions from Update()
- **Strict limit**: If a case in `Update(msg tea.Msg)` exceeds **5 lines**, extract it into a separate function
- **Naming**: `handle[MessageType]` (e.g. `handleContextSwitch()`, `handleKeyPress()`)
- **Pattern**: The function must return `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)`

**Before (bad):**
```go
case ContextSwitchCompleteMsg:
    a.config = msg.Config
    a.currentContext = msg.ContextName
    a.reinitializeViews(msg.Config)
    return a, func() tea.Msg {
        return tea.WindowSizeMsg{Width: a.width, Height: a.height}
    }
```

**After (good):**
```go
case ContextSwitchCompleteMsg:
    return a.handleContextSwitch(msg)

// Further down in the file
func (a *App) handleContextSwitch(msg ContextSwitchCompleteMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
    a.config = msg.Config
    a.currentContext = msg.ContextName
    a.reinitializeViews(msg.Config)
    return a, func() tea.Msg {
        return tea.WindowSizeMsg{Width: a.width, Height: a.height}
    }
}
```

#### Code reuse
- **Zero duplication**: If a block of code appears 2+ times, create a function
- **Modules**: Group related functions together (e.g. all context switching in a single file)
- **Constants**: Extract magic values into named constants

#### Error handling
- **Bubble Tea pattern**: Errors = messages (e.g. `ContextSwitchErrorMsg`)
- **Always log** in DEBUG mode: `log.Printf("ERROR: %v", err)`
- **Never ignore**: If the error is non-critical, document why

#### Comments
- **Mandatory for**:
  - Exported (public) functions
  - Complex business logic
  - Workarounds or non-obvious decisions
- **Format**: `// functionName does X and returns Y`
- **Avoid**: Comments that repeat the code

#### Complexity
- **Maximum 3 levels of indentation** in a function
- **Functions > 50 lines**: refactor into smaller functions
- **Switch > 10 cases**: consider a table-driven pattern

## Code editing instructions

### Rule 201 : Code must be clean, concise, and well-structured to stay maintainable

#### Extracting functions from Update()
- **Strict limit**: If a case in `Update(msg tea.Msg)` exceeds **5 lines**, extract it into a separate function
- **Naming**: `handle[MessageType]` (e.g. `handleContextSwitch()`, `handleKeyPress()`)
- **Pattern**: The function must return `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)`

**Before (bad):**
```go
case ContextSwitchCompleteMsg:
    a.config = msg.Config
    a.currentContext = msg.ContextName
    a.reinitializeViews(msg.Config)
    return a, func() tea.Msg {
        return tea.WindowSizeMsg{Width: a.width, Height: a.height}
    }
```

**After (good):**
```go
case ContextSwitchCompleteMsg:
    return a.handleContextSwitch(msg)

// Further down in the file
func (a *App) handleContextSwitch(msg ContextSwitchCompleteMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
    a.config = msg.Config
    a.currentContext = msg.ContextName
    a.reinitializeViews(msg.Config)
    return a, func() tea.Msg {
        return tea.WindowSizeMsg{Width: a.width, Height: a.height}
    }
}
```

#### Code reuse
- **Zero duplication**: If a block of code appears 2+ times, create a function
- **Modules**: Group related functions together (e.g. all context switching in a single file)
- **Constants**: Extract magic values into named constants

#### Error handling
- **Bubble Tea pattern**: Errors = messages (e.g. `ContextSwitchErrorMsg`)
- **Always log** in DEBUG mode: `log.Printf("ERROR: %v", err)`
- **Never ignore**: If the error is non-critical, document why

#### Comments
- **Mandatory for**:
  - Exported (public) functions
  - Complex business logic
  - Workarounds or non-obvious decisions
- **Format**: `// functionName does X and returns Y`
- **Avoid**: Comments that repeat the code

#### Complexity
- **Maximum 3 levels of indentation** in a function
- **Functions > 50 lines**: refactor into smaller functions
- **Switch > 10 cases**: consider a table-driven pattern

# TUI — Bubble Tea behavior & architecture

### Rule 109 : Bubble Tea message naming convention

- Format: `[ComponentName][Action]Msg`
- Examples: `ComponentFormSubmitMsg`, `ConfirmModalYesMsg`
- Always document with a comment
- Group related messages together in the file

### Rule 110 : NEVER modify the model inside a Cmd ⚠️

**Fundamental principle of Bubble Tea (Elm architecture).**

`Update()`, `View()`, and `Cmd`s execute in parallel. Modifying the model inside a Cmd creates race conditions detectable with `go run -race`.

| Component | Role | Can modify the model? |
|-----------|------|---------------------------|
| `Update()` | Processes messages | ✅ YES (the only allowed place) |
| `View()` | Renders the UI | ❌ NO (read-only) |
| `Cmd` | Async I/O operations | ❌ NO (returns messages) |

| `nexus-bench:status` | `... status` | reads only |
| `nexus-bench:render` | `... render` | no, contacts nothing |

per `NEXUS_BENCH_*` variable: `--context`, `--namespace`, `--http-nodeport`,
`--docker-nodeport`, `--cpu-request`, `--cpu-limit`, `--memory-request`,
`--memory-limit`, `--storage-size`, `--jvm-opts`, `--image`, `--image-tag`,
`--upstream-url`, `--anonymous`, `--hosts`, `--timeout`, `--delete-timeout`,
`--secrets`, `--descriptor`. `up` and `provision` add `--accept-eula` and
`--rest-host`. Each subcommand has its own `flag.FlagSet` (`ContinueOnError`,
output discarded: the command prints parse errors itself on stderr and `-h` on
stdout). A flag is laid over its variable and the result goes through
`FromEnv(Defaults(), ...)` once, so "flag, then `NEXUS_BENCH_*`, then default",
the parsing and the rule that `--namespace` moves the upstream URL (unless an

step failed, a run cancelled); `2` mistake in the command line (no or unknown

a `BenchError` (also when wrapped by `%w` or joined) prints exactly its

trace); a cancelled run says `cancelled` and that `status` shows where things

successful `Provision`**, never on a failure at any step, and a descriptor from
an earlier run is left as it was. It is built with `BuildDescriptor(p,

- **Exit codes:**
  - 0: success, and `help`/`-h`.
  - 1: invalid parameters, a failed step, a cancelled run, or an invalid `--rest-host`.
  - 2: usage errors: no or unknown subcommand, unknown flag, bad type, missing value, extra argument.

- **Descriptor:** written only after `Provision` succeeds, and left untouched on any failure.

- **Status output:** `status` prints four findings (`bench:`, `pod:`, `rest:`, `descriptor:`) and exits 0. It exits 1 only when the preflight fails, for example `NamespaceMissing` or an unreachable cluster. A failed `kubectl get pods` or a failed probe is reported as a finding with no error text. Descriptor drift is checked on context, namespace, image, both NodePorts, upstream URL and the anonymous flag. Hosts and versions are left out because they come from the cluster.
- **Flags per subcommand:** `--accept-eula` and `--rest-host` exist only on `up` and `provision`. The other subcommands accept every parameter flag, because the tests give `--namespace`, `--context` and so on to `down`, `status` and `render`.
- **Not done:** step 9 (the integration tests and source guards) and step 10 (the real run). `nexus-bench:test` runs `-run Integration`, which matches no test until step 9.
